## Text

```
Links Platform planned as a system, that combines simple associative memory storage (Links) and transformation execution engine (Triggers). There will be an ability to program that system dynamically, due to the fact that all algorithms will be treated as data inside the storage. Such algorithms can also change themselves in real-time based on input from the environment. The Links Platform is a method of modeling the high-level associative memory effects of human mind.

We strive to make our implementation of associative storage the most accurate, simple, universal, flexible, reliable and fast memory implementation for any data and knowledge.

One of the most important goals of the project is to accelerate the development of automation to the level when automation can be itself automated.
```

## Description

The translation is not fully correct, and also formalization of the result is not fully correct.

When I select options for questions, they don't look having affect on actual translation.

See full questions and translation steps in: https://gist.github.com/konard/7b6495c6a5deb8aa4207052f0ea17ba1

We need to find root cause of all 404 errors and fix it.

We need to ensure we have smart cache system.

First of all I see to many repeated requests to definitions like `https://en.wiktionary.org/api/rest_v1/page/definition/for`

Also urls like `API request: GET https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbgetentities&format=json&ids=Q36978172&languages=en&origin=*&props=labels%7Caliases%7Cdescriptions%7Cclaims%7Csitelinks&sitefilter=enwiki` suggets, that they support multiple ids, and we only use one of them.

We should try to reduce number of requests by grouping them as possible.

We also should execute requests in parallel, unless we have errors about API rate limit like 429. We need to make sure we slow down only when we get 429's, and once we don't have them for at least a minute we can speed up again and use up to 8 requests in parallel speeding up gradualy each 15 seconds (the same should be done at the start). Like 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 each 15 seconds.

Also even if we group loading of entities into single request, we should store them in cache as if we requested separately. And we should make sure cache lives at least 7 days + random 1-3 days, so not all all items are invalidated from cache at the same time.

So we should at the same time fix all the bugs, reduce load to APIs by caching data, and reusing cache between page reload, by storing in local storage, indexdb and so on.

Also we should so smart passes of each step, doing actual collection of data we need to request in single batch, start requesting, get all the requets finished, continue thinking on translation steps, collecting new batch of data to be requested and so on.

Make sure everything is implemented in both Rust and JavaScript, and by default we use Rust web assembly background worker, with ability to switch to JavaScript background worker. UI must not be blocked at any time, but we should block translate button and put translating status inside the button itself, so it should be not possible to produce new events that will break current execution. Also to make user see some progress we can move translation steps section up (after the button), and in collapsed state show how many steps executed vs planned, it is ok, that planned steps increase dynamycally. In the expanded more all steps are written in details (human readable please, with all requests and responses also expandable if needed). I want all the steps be trully transparrent.

While you make fixes, make sure we solve general formalization/naturalization algorithms, to drive the highest possible quality of translation possible. So we prefer general solutions, which also support all existing test cases, if test cases can be improved do so, but only if much better.

Also we need a switch to check the priority of formalization, by default we should use wikipedia article, if not exists check wikidata item, and if not exists in there either go with wiktionary. But that priority should be changable, and we should produce fake ids of articles with WP prefix, and fake ids with WK prefix for wiktionary. So the result of formalization is always ids, that always convertible to either link to wikipedia or wikidata or wiktionary.

We need to continue on our vision based on requirements from
Previously we worked on quality in
- https://github.com/link-assistant/meta-expression/issues/50
- https://github.com/link-assistant/meta-expression/issues/43
- https://github.com/link-assistant/meta-expression/issues/48
- https://github.com/link-assistant/meta-expression/issues/35
- and other issues

We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
